idiom_name: tagged frame header (enum tag + length) switched on before the body is decoded
implementation_notes: C has no runtime type information and no standard serializer, so the full structure is hand-written: a fixed header (tag, length) or a self-describing codec such as CBOR supplies the discriminator, and a switch on the tag selects the decoder for the body. An in-process C99 tagged union (enum tag plus a union member) is the in-memory form of the same idea; on the wire the tag must be an explicit field of a byte-ordered header, not a memory dump of a struct. The classic table of {tag, decode function} pairs is still worth writing once more than a handful of types share a channel, because it is the only thing that makes the tag vocabulary explicit and testable.
pitfalls: Casting the wire buffer to a struct relies on layout, padding and alignment; read header fields with explicit byte-order accessors instead of memcpy-ing structs, or the same bytes parse differently across ABIs and packed types.
switch exhaustiveness is not checked: a tag missing from the table silently becomes the default path, so route default to a dead-letter bucket and test the tag vocabulary.

The tag and the length field both come from the payload; validate the declared length against the remaining buffer before decoding, because an untrusted tag with an unchecked length is the classic over-read.
